description: Write a Python ETL script (requests + pandas) for saas_metrics that ingests all records from a cursor-paginated REST endpoint GET /v1/accounts?cursor=<cursor>&limit=2. Each response has the shape {data: [...], next_cursor: string or null}. The script should: (1) follow next_cursor until it is null, (2) guard against an endless loop when the API returns the same cursor twice, (3) deduplicate records on id because rows can shift between pages while paginating, (4) convert created_at from epoch seconds to UTC timestamps, (5) write the result to Parquet. The sample shows the two page responses.
edge_cases: id 2 appears on both pages and must be loaded once
Termination must be driven by next_cursor being null, not by a page having fewer than 'limit' rows or by an empty page
A repeated cursor must abort with an error instead of looping forever
created_at is in seconds; passing it to pd.to_datetime without unit='s' interprets it as nanoseconds (1970 dates)
A non-200 response in the middle of pagination must fail the run rather than write a partial file
common_failure_modes: FM7: Partial result written as if complete after a mid-pagination error
FM4: Epoch seconds interpreted as nanoseconds or milliseconds
FM3: Duplicates across pages inflate downstream counts
